## Tours to Moray: what to compare before choosing

[Moray](/peru/place/moray/) lies in the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) region, northwest of [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). Stone terraces descend in concentric rings into natural depressions. Differences in conditions at successive levels suggest agricultural experimentation by the Incas, although the site's precise purpose remains a subject of research.

Our collection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Moray on the main itinerary. They share a visit to this archaeological site but differ in how busy the day is, their overall duration and the cities or countries visited afterward. It is especially useful to check whether Moray is combined with the [Maras salt pans](/peru/place/maras/) and [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/): these are separate stops even if a tour operator groups them together under "Sacred Valley."

## Moray and Maras: why they offer different experiences

At [Moray](/peru/place/moray/), visitors see circular terraces and the terrain used by Inca builders. [Maras](/peru/place/maras/) is known for salt-evaporation ponds on a hillside: their appearance, layout and economic use are completely different. Both sites fit into one part of a Sacred Valley excursion, but a short day may include only one.

For example, on the [private Inca Deluxe tour](/peru/tour/peru-inca-deluxe-8-days/), a day is devoted to Ollantaytambo, Moray and Maras, and lunch at Mil Centro is included. On the [Belmond Hiram Bingham train journey](/peru/tour/peru-belmond-hiram-bingham-machu-picchu/), the valley day combines [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/), Moray and Ollantaytambo. The geography is similar, but the programs organize time in the region differently. Do not transfer meals, transport or other inclusions from one tour to another; compare the actual itinerary you choose.

Visiting Moray involves more than a quick photograph. Take time to walk along the permitted viewing areas, study the concentric terrace system from several angles and hear about Inca agriculture. The exact route through the complex and trail access depend on current visiting rules.

## How to fit Moray into a Peru journey

### A short introduction: Cusco, the valley and Machu Picchu

The [six-day Peru tour](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-6-days/) concentrates on [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). One day is dedicated to the Sacred Valley, with [Pisac](/peru/place/pisac/), Ollantaytambo, Chinchero and Moray among the stops. This suits travelers hoping to see Inca heritage with limited time.

A busy sightseeing day requires careful planning of the stops. If a detailed introduction to ancient agriculture and an unhurried look at the terraces matter to you, compare this with longer itineraries allowing more time in the valley.

### A journey with a special train section

On [Inca Deluxe](/peru/tour/peru-inca-deluxe-8-days/), the Hiram Bingham train is used for the journey to Machu Picchu, while Moray is visited on a separate day together with other Sacred Valley sites. This distinction matters: the train serves a different part of the trip and does not automatically reduce the road travel needed to reach the terraces.

The [six-day Belmond program](/peru/tour/peru-belmond-hiram-bingham-machu-picchu/) also dedicates a day to "Chinchero, Moray and Ollantaytambo." Compare not only the train name but also the order of days, overnight accommodation, included excursions and time allocated to archaeological sites.

### An extended itinerary through Peru or several countries

On the [21-day Peru journey](/peru/tour/best-of-peru-21-days/), Moray comes after the coast around [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/), the Nazca Lines, Lake Titicaca and other Andean stops. The program reveals the diversity of natural environments and archaeological sites within one country.

On the [group tour through Brazil, Peru and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/), Moray is part of the Peruvian section of a much wider itinerary. This format is convenient for seeing several countries in one journey, but usually leaves less time per site than a trip devoted to southern Peru alone.

## What to consider when planning your day

**Altitude and acclimatization.** Moray lies in the highlands near Cusco, more than 3,000 m above sea level. If you arrive from sea level, a gentler start to the Andes, drinking water and time to adjust are useful. Individual tolerance to altitude varies. Continuing strenuous activity during significant illness without assessing your condition is dangerous.

**Transfers.** Moray, Chinchero, Maras, Pisac and Ollantaytambo occupy different parts of the valley. Their appearance in a tour title does not mean they can all be seen without rushing. Check the day-by-day order, number of stops and whether you return to Cusco or stay overnight in the valley.

**Season.** In the Andes, a generally drier season runs roughly from May to September and a rainier one from November to March, with variable conditions in between. In clear weather, terraces and mountains are sharply visible; after rainfall, stone paths may be slippery. Check the actual forecast and access rules before departure.

**Tickets.** Exactly which entrance tickets, guiding and transportation are included depends on the chosen tour. Tourist ticket packages and archaeological site access conditions can change; confirm them when planning rather than inferring them from "tour to Moray."

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Moray

### How much time is needed at Moray?

Visiting the concentric terraces usually takes part of a day in the Sacred Valley. The full excursion's duration depends on other stops. To see Moray, Maras and Ollantaytambo together, choose a program with a dedicated day in the valley.

### Are Moray and Maras the same place?

No. Moray is a complex of circular archaeological terraces; Maras is a settlement and area famous for salt pans. Tours often combine them, but each site's inclusion should be checked separately.

### Can I visit Moray before Machu Picchu?

Yes, some current itineraries follow that order. Others visit the valley after Machu Picchu, so rely on the full day-by-day program.

### Is Moray included in a short six-day tour?

Yes. The [Lima, Cusco and Machu Picchu itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-6-days/) includes Moray among the stops during its Sacred Valley day. The trip's total duration does not tell you how much time is allocated to the site.

### Can Moray be combined with other interests?

Yes. If your journey centers on Inca history, see [cultural and historical tours in Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/). If you need a specific route through Moray, compare the tours above and confirm their stops.

## Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands: two different experiences in Peru

This destination page brings together two attractions on the Pacific coast of [Peru](/peru/). **The Nazca Lines** are huge figures on the desert surface, created by pre-Hispanic cultures. **The Ballestas Islands** are a protected marine area near Paracas where visitors observe sea lions, birds and sometimes Humboldt penguins.

The practical point is that the two sites lie **in different parts of the Ica department**. Seeing the lines from the air and making a sea trip to the islands require separate journeys, different forms of transport and attention to weather.

## The Nazca Lines: what can be seen from the air?

The Nazca and Palpa geoglyphs are known for hummingbird, monkey, spider and other bird designs, along with numerous straight lines and geometric figures. According to UNESCO, this tradition existed for many centuries from the pre-Christian era into the early centuries CE. The site was added to the World Heritage List in 1994.

The figures were made by removing dark surface stones to expose the lighter ground beneath. Many designs are easiest to appreciate from above because of their vast size. However, saying that "all the lines can only be seen from a plane" is inaccurate: certain features are visible from viewing points on land.

A **sightseeing flight** is a separate aviation service. Which figures are visible depends on the route, weather and flight restrictions. Travelers susceptible to motion sickness should consider the aircraft's turns and ask the operator for advice in advance.

## Ballestas Islands: sea lions and birds

The [Ballestas Islands](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/) lie off the coast of Paracas and form part of Peru's national protected system of islands and guano headlands. Sea lions and numerous seabirds, including boobies and cormorants, inhabit the rocks; Humboldt penguins can sometimes be seen.

Tour boats usually depart from the El Chaco area of Paracas. On the way, they often pass the **Paracas Candelabra**, a large geoglyph on a coastal slope. It can be seen from the water, although the symbol's origins remain debated.

Ordinary sightseeing tours do not include landing on the protected islands. The principal aim is observing wildlife from a vessel at an appropriate distance. A light windproof jacket and protection from splashes and sun are useful. Departures depend on sea conditions and the maritime authorities' decisions.

## Combining Nazca and Ballestas

| Site | How to visit |
|---|---|
| Nazca geoglyphs | Aerial tour or land-based viewpoints |
| Ballestas Islands | Boat excursion from Paracas |
| Candelabra | View from the water en route to the islands |

Choose the sequence of transfers first. Heading south from Lima, you encounter Paracas before Nazca. For the flight, confirm the departure airfield and time; for the boat, the pier, morning departure slot and a weather buffer.

Trying to combine both experiences in one day without a precise transport plan is risky: Paracas and Nazca are separated by several hours of road travel. Separate stops with an overnight stay or a prearranged coastal itinerary can be more convenient.

When browsing [Peru tours](/peru/tour/), check the actual activities: mention of Nazca does not prove an aerial excursion is included, and the name Paracas alone does not confirm a boat trip to Ballestas.

## Protecting archaeology and wildlife

UNESCO regards the geoglyphs as a vulnerable cultural landscape. Do not drive over the figures or stray from permitted routes: vehicle and foot traffic can damage the surface. For an independent land visit, use officially authorized viewpoints.

Wildlife protection rules apply at the islands. Do not feed birds, throw objects into the water or make loud noises; follow the crew's instructions. A good wildlife experience is based on watching animals behave naturally, rather than trying to get as close to a colony as possible.

## Frequently asked questions about the Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands

### Can I see the Nazca Lines without flying?

Some geoglyphs and lines are visible from designated land-based viewpoints. To see many of the large figures, travelers generally choose an aerial excursion.

### Can you land on the Ballestas Islands?

Ordinary tourist trips involve observing them from a boat. The islands are a protected natural area, so unrestricted landing is not permitted.

### What's the difference between the Candelabra and the Nazca Lines?

The Candelabra lies on a slope of the Paracas Peninsula and is visible from the sea. The principal Nazca geoglyphs lie considerably farther south, on dry plateaus.

## Nazca Lines and Ballestas: adding both destinations to your itinerary

We have grouped the [Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/) in one geographical section because some excursions feature them in sequence. **However, the islands and the geoglyphs are separate places requiring different transport**: boats depart for the islands from [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/), while the Nazca Lines are usually seen from the air.

If the main journey centers on [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Lake Titicaca, the Pacific extension must be planned as a separate stage with transfers. The [Multifaceted Peru tour](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/) offers an additional trip to Paracas and Nazca. The option also exists on certain [Peru and Bolivia itineraries](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/), although its format differs.

Here are programs where Paracas, Ballestas or Nazca are **possible additions**. If both the sea and aerial stages must be mandatory, explore [tours visiting these places on the main itinerary](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/tour/).

## Two very different experiences on one trip

The Ballestas Islands belong to a protected marine zone off Peru's coast. According to the Peruvian protected areas authority, SERNANP, sea lions, numerous seabirds and Humboldt penguins live here. Tour boats pass among rocks and arches, with the coast and wildlife observed from the water. On the way from Paracas, there may be a view of the large Candelabra geoglyph on the peninsula's slope.

[Nazca](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/) is another story: immense drawings and geometric lines on a dry plain in southern Peru. The Nazca and Palpa geoglyphs are a UNESCO World Heritage property. Their size and relative positions are easier to grasp from above. A [flight over the Nazca Lines](/peru/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/nazca-lines-flight/) therefore differs from a land-based coastal excursion.

| Stage | Main experience |
|---|---|
| [Ballestas](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/) | Boat trip and marine wildlife |
| Candelabra | View from the sea |
| Nazca Lines | Sightseeing flight |

Because the experiences differ, a combined journey must account both for boat operating conditions at sea and suitable weather for the flight. Merely having a free day in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) does not guarantee that both activities can take place.

## Optional formats in Ada Tours itineraries

On the [12-day Peru journey covering Cusco, Titicaca and Arequipa](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/), the marine outing and Nazca are offered separately from the main days. This extension makes sense if you are prepared to devote substantial time to the coast after visiting the Andes, rather than treating it as a brief Lima city excursion.

The [Captivating Peru and Iquitos itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-iquitos-discovery/) also offers an additional full day covering Paracas, the Ballestas Islands and a flight over the Nazca Lines. The price of this option in that particular tour is **$625**. The main journey spans the Andes and Amazon, so coordinate the early departure with flight days and rest after intensive stages.

On the [Peru and Bolivia with Uyuni Salt Flats tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/), there are **two distinct formats**: a two-day, one-night optional trip to Paracas and Nazca, or a full-day tour including the Ballestas Islands and Nazca Lines. The full-day option costs **$550 net per person**; the two-day option is priced separately, with the Nazca flight charged extra. These prices and service inclusions belong to different options and must not be merged into a single rate.

See the standalone excursions for full details: [full-day Paracas–Ballestas–Nazca](/peru/paracas/peru-paracas-nazca-full-day/) or [Paracas and Nazca over two days](/peru/paracas/paracas-nazca-two-days/). Each must be considered alongside your main tour, actual date and transport connections.

## Key constraints: time, sea and aviation

**What matters most is not the tour's total duration but how much time is actually available in Lima before an international departure or after returning from other regions.** Some itineraries include part of a free day, but an early departure to Paracas, the boat trip, onward travel and a sightseeing flight demand a substantial time window. The two-day option also requires an additional overnight stay.

The boat trip depends on sea conditions, wind and the relevant authorities. The desert flight depends on weather, visibility, scheduling and each passenger's tolerance for flying. Weather suitable for Ballestas does not always mean weather suitable for Nazca. Before booking, establish what happens if one stage is canceled, whether the return transfer to Lima is included and what rescheduling conditions apply.

To protect marine wildlife, follow the guides' instructions, wear a life jacket and do not feed the animals. Around archaeological geoglyphs, observe access rules and stay within permitted areas. Check admission fees and other payments against the terms of **the specific** excursion; do not assume every option has the same inclusions.

## Choosing between a day trip and a dedicated coastal stage

If the Nazca Lines are your main interest, first confirm that a sightseeing flight can operate and under what conditions; visiting Ballestas is not a substitute. If you want to see seabirds, marine mammals and the rocky shore, Paracas is the principal stage. For both experiences, choose a program with enough time rather than inserting complex travel between tightly scheduled flights.

A two-day option relieves some pressure from one very long day, but adds an overnight stay and changes the overall trip duration. A full-day excursion saves calendar time but involves intensive transfers. Compare [the main Peru tours](/peru/tour/) and the full description of your chosen [Paracas–Nazca excursion](/peru/paracas/peru-paracas-nazca-full-day/) before deciding.

## Frequently asked questions about optional Nazca and Ballestas trips

### Are the Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands close together?

They lie in different parts of southern Peru's coast. Boat excursions leave from around Paracas; the Nazca Lines lie farther south in the desert. A combined visit requires separate road transfers.

### Is the Nazca flight included in every two-day option?

No. On the [two-day extension of the Peru and Bolivia with Uyuni program](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/), the flight is listed as an additional expense. Other excursion inclusions may differ; check the actual option.

### Can a boat trip and flight be guaranteed on a chosen date?

No. Both stages depend on weather and operating schedules. Check availability and rescheduling rules separately before confirming the program.

### Is it worth allowing two days instead of one?

If a calmer pace and more time between the sea excursion and the flight over Nazca matter to you, a two-day trip may be more convenient. When time is limited, consider the [full-day Paracas–Nazca tour](/peru/paracas/peru-paracas-nazca-full-day/), but confirm the entire transport sequence first.

## Choosing a tour of the Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands

The [Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/) are grouped in one travel destination but lie in different places. The Nazca Lines consist of drawings of animals and plants and geometric figures on the desert surface. The Ballestas Islands lie in the Pacific off [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/): boats take visitors near the rocks to see sea lions, birds and Humboldt penguins.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with this destination in their travel geography. **Mentioning Nazca and Ballestas does not guarantee that a flight and boat trip are included in the base itinerary.** Some tours devote separate days to the coast, while others offer these excursions only if extra time is added to the main Andean route. | [Southern Peru in 12 days](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/) | Paracas and Nazca flight listed as extras |

## Flight over the Nazca Lines or a land-based visit?

The Lines and Geoglyphs of Nazca and Palpa are a UNESCO World Heritage property. Certain figures, including the famous hummingbird, monkey and spider, are much easier to see from above. A dedicated viewing tower offers a limited view of part of the plateau. These experiences are quite different.

To see the figures from a plane, look for an explicit **flight over the Nazca Lines** on the itinerary. A land-based stop at a viewpoint does not replace it. Visibility and airfield operating conditions affect flights. Travelers on small planes should also consider turns and potential motion sickness.

On the [21-day Peru journey](/peru/tour/best-of-peru-21-days/), the coastal portion follows a logical sequence: a drive from [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) to Paracas, the island excursion, then [Ica](/peru/place/ica/) and Nazca. This allows time to experience the coast as a separate stage before continuing to [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/) and the Andes.

## Ballestas Islands: marine life near Paracas

Boats for the Ballestas Islands depart from the Paracas area. Sea lions and bird colonies, including pelicans and Humboldt penguins, live on and around the rocks. From the sea, travelers can also see the Paracas Candelabra, a geoglyph on a coastal sandy slope that is geographically separate from the Nazca Lines.

Wind and swell matter on the sea excursion. Animal numbers, viewing distances and even departure conditions cannot be guaranteed: this is wildlife observation. If the boat trip is especially important to you, choose an itinerary with a time buffer on the coast and check rescheduling or cancellation arrangements.

[Pisco](/peru/place/pisco/) and Paracas serve as bases for coastal itineraries. Travelers often combine them with Ica, but a boat to Ballestas and an aerial view of Nazca have separate logistics. They cannot be treated as one short stop.

## How the Ada Tours programs differ

### A comprehensive route through Peru

[Best of Peru in 21 Days](/peru/tour/best-of-peru-21-days/) combines the coast with [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/), [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Amazonia. The boat excursion to Ballestas and onward journey via Ica to Nazca are set out on separate days. This option suits travelers who want to see Peru's diverse natural regions in one trip.

### A VIP trip with private aviation

On the [18-day Peru and Bolivia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/), a special day is dedicated to the Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands. The flight toward Nazca uses a Grand Caravan, followed by Pisco and Paracas, while a private yacht takes the group to the islands. These details belong to this particular tour. Another product labeled VIP does not automatically include the same services.

### A short Peru trip with optional excursions

On the [eight-day itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-8-days/), the main stops are Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Puno. Paracas, Ballestas and Nazca are listed as possible additions on free days. If seeing the Nazca Lines is your central goal, confirm the necessary itinerary changes and additional cost in advance.

On the [southern Peru program](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/), the names Nazca and Paracas also appear, but the visits are marked optional. Read the relevant day's description instead of relying on the tour title.

## How much time to allow on the coast?

To combine marine and aerial excursions, allow time for road travel, the boat trip and the flight. The route commonly runs through Lima, Paracas, Ica and the Nazca area. There is an overland journey between the ocean and the desert plateau, so attempting everything in only a few hours makes the plan vulnerable to traffic and weather.

The Peruvian coast has a climate very different from high-altitude Cusco. Strong winds in Paracas may affect sea conditions, while visibility is essential for the flight over Nazca. If the journey then continues into the Andes, assess flight time and acclimatization separately.

Wildlife lovers can compare [nature tours in Peru](/interests/wildlife/tours/peru/). If archaeology and geoglyphs interest you more, explore [Peru's cultural and historical routes](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/). These sections cover far more than the Nazca–Ballestas combination.

## Before your trip

Confirm the two excursions independently: whether the flight is included and where it departs, the type of boat, admission and port fees, and the number of nights on the coast. Check the conditions for changing dates if the weather is unfavorable. Families with children and people prone to motion sickness should discuss transport and the actual operator's restrictions in advance.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are the Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands close together?

No. The Nazca Lines are in the desert, while Ballestas lies offshore near Paracas. Tourist itineraries connect the two by road.

### Can the geoglyphs be seen without flying?

Some drawings are visible from a viewing tower. A sightseeing flight is used to see many of the larger figures. These are two different options.

### Can visitors see penguins at the islands?

Yes. Humboldt penguins live around the Ballestas Islands, along with sea lions and many seabirds. Actual sightings depend on nature.

### Does every tour in this catalog include both excursions?

No. Some itineraries list Paracas and Nazca as optional additions. Compare the mandatory days with separately paid services.

### What is different about the VIP itinerary?

The specific [18-day program](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-amazon-cruise-vip-18-days/) specifies a private plane and yacht. Other VIP trips have their own terms.

## Ollantaytambo in Peru: Inca town, terraces and the road to Machu Picchu

Ollantaytambo lies in the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), in Peru's Cusco Department. It combines a living town with old streets and water channels and a large archaeological complex on the mountainside. Inca heritage is visible both in the monuments and in the everyday urban environment.

During one visit, you can walk narrow stone streets, study the old masonry of residential blocks and climb terraces to monumental stone structures. Unlike a brief stop at a viewpoint, Ollantaytambo is best appreciated by exploring **the town below and the archaeological complex higher up the slope** in sequence.

## Two sides of Ollantaytambo: town and archaeological complex

The historic town retains a distinctive rectangular block layout, stone walls and water channels running beside the streets. Houses, shops and small squares occupy these quarters. Walking among them offers a view of how a settlement continues to function within a centuries-old urban layout.

Above the town lie stepped terraces and an archaeological complex often called Ollantaytambo Fortress. It includes ceremonial spaces, stone walls and structures serving different purposes within the Inca center.

| Area | What you can see |
|---|---|
| Old town quarters | Inca walls and channels |
| Hillside complex | Terraces, stairs and temples |

The two parts call for different kinds of visits. You can walk in the town without climbing to the upper terraces. The archaeological zone requires more time and physical effort.

## Terraces, stonework and the Temple of the Sun

Broad stone terraces rise along the hillside, creating one of Ollantaytambo's most recognizable views. Their construction served agricultural and engineering purposes, although the complex also held ceremonial significance. Stone walls created stable levels on steep terrain.

Higher up stand monumental blocks associated with the **Temple of the Sun**. The enormous, carefully shaped stones placed side by side are particularly impressive. They demonstrate the Inca builders' ability to transport and fit stone without modern construction equipment.

Water engineering is another highlight: channels, fountains and intricate sections of stone waterworks. Working channels are still visible in the town, making Inca engineering something visitors can observe directly.

## Manco Inca and the defense of the town

Ollantaytambo is also known for events during the Spanish conquest. Manco Inca took refuge here in the 16th century and organized resistance against the conquistadors. In 1536, Inca forces resisted troops commanded by Hernando Pizarro. This history helps explain why the site is often called a fortress, although it served far more than military purposes.

When sightseeing, keep both periods in mind: the construction of the monumental center during the Inca state's development, and its role during the conquest. The terraces and defensive areas then become part of a larger account of Andean history.

## Where Ollantaytambo is and how to get there

The town lies in the Urubamba River valley at approximately **2,790 m**. Visitors travel here from [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) by car through the Sacred Valley as part of excursions or multi-day tours. The stop combines well with other valley destinations, but the actual sites and order of transfers depend on the itinerary.

Ollantaytambo is also an important **railway hub en route to Machu Picchu**. Tourists board trains here for Machu Picchu Pueblo, from where they continue to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Simply changing trains does not mean a guided tour of Ollantaytambo's archaeological complex: plan these activities separately.

If you want to see both historical sites, compare the time required for Ollantaytambo with your Machu Picchu tickets in advance. Staying overnight in the Sacred Valley can help spread the physical demands across more than one day.

## Preparing for the walk and climb

Comfortable footwear and adequate time for steps are essential for the upper archaeological complex. The altitude is lower than in Cusco, but this is still the Andean highlands. Sunshine can be strong, and weather can change during the day.

Bring water, a hat and a warm layer. If climbing the terraces is difficult, spend more time exploring the town and its lower water channels. A comfortable pace matters more than completing every section quickly.

## Frequently asked questions about Ollantaytambo

### Is Ollantaytambo a town or a fortress?

Both. The name refers to the modern settlement with its Inca street plan and the archaeological complex of terraces and temples on the hillside.

### Why is the Temple of the Sun famous?

For the large, carefully shaped stone blocks associated with its ceremonial complex. The masonry demonstrates the skill of Inca builders.

### Can I travel from Ollantaytambo to Machu Picchu?

Yes. Trains depart from here toward Machu Picchu Pueblo. The actual tickets, timetable and onward journey depend on your selected itinerary.
